_meta.what: Materials a 2026 F1 car can be built from (and a few it cannot), with the properties the concept part-mass model uses. Read by concept/materials.js (which embeds an identical copy for the browser; test/concept-coupling.test.js proves they match).
_meta.contract: entries are { id, name, class, form, density_kg_m3, E_GPa, tensile_MPa, typical_f1_use, kind, basis, fia: { article, status, note, verified }, sources: [source id] } plus class-specific fields (fibre for laminates, li_wt_pct / be_wt_pct for alloys). A design part may carry params.material = "<id>" (concept/parts.js MATERIAL_PARTS says which parts and which forms).
_meta.units: density kg/m³; E in GPa; tensile (ultimate) in MPa. Laminates: in-plane quasi-isotropic laminate values (see laminate_rule). Cores: out-of-plane (flatwise) stabilised compressive modulus and strength.
_meta.laminate_rule: Laminate entries (60 % fibre volume, epoxy) start from the maker's unidirectional (UD) composite data (ASTM D3039, normalised to 60 % Vf). Quasi-isotropic [0/±45/90]s values are an ENGINEERING ESTIMATE: E_QI ≈ 3/8·E1 + 5/8·E2 (the classical quasi-isotropic approximation for E1 ≫ E2; E2 from the stated transverse modulus estimate), tensile_QI ≈ 0.33 × UD tensile strength (estimate). Laminate density = 0.6 × fibre density + 0.4 × 1220 kg/m³ (cured epoxy, estimate).
_meta.fia_note: fia.* records this module's reading of FIA 2026 Section C Article C15 (Materials) and the part-specific material articles, Issue 19 (25/06/2026, in force at Silverstone), text extracted from the fia.com PDF on 2026-10-24. verified=false throughout: the FIA-checklist helper verifies these and owns the legality check (concept/regs.js). Statuses: permitted (listed in C15.2), specific_use (permitted only for named components), forbidden, not_listed (not in the exhaustive C15.2 list, so not permitted outside the PU unless added under C15.1.5/C15.1.6).
_meta.honesty: Typical / datasheet values, not design allowables, not measured on any F1 part. Every number has a source id or kind 'engineering estimate'.

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy prepreg, standard modulus (T700S class), quasi-isotropic
materials.typical_f1_use: secondary structure, bodywork, tooling-friendly panels
materials.kind: datasheet UD values + engineering estimate (QI rule)

fia.note: PAN carbon fibre with nominal tensile modulus ≤ 550 GPa, tensile strength ≤ 7100 MPa, density ≤ 1.92 g/cm³; epoxy matrix

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy prepreg, intermediate modulus (T800S class), quasi-isotropic
materials.typical_f1_use: concept baseline for wings, floor, bodywork, wishbones, gearbox casing
materials.kind: datasheet UD values + engineering estimate (QI rule)

fia.note: PAN carbon fibre inside the C15.2.3(b)(i) modulus / strength / density limits

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy prepreg, ultra-high strength (T1100G class), quasi-isotropic
materials.typical_f1_use: concept baseline for the survival cell skins and impact structures (C15.5.3 requires CC-UHS plies, fibre Ftu > 6250 MPa)
materials.kind: datasheet UD values + engineering estimate (QI rule)

fia.note: 7000 MPa fibre: under the 7100 MPa cap ('up to and including Toray T1100') and above the 6250 MPa CC-UHS fibre threshold; CC-UHS is a woven carbon cloth epoxy prepreg (C15.5.1(f)), so the fibre qualifies for the homologated survival-cell laminates in woven-cloth form (this row is a quasi-isotropic laminate: wording only, no verdict change)

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy prepreg, high modulus (M55J class), quasi-isotropic
materials.typical_f1_use: stiffness-critical parts (wing main planes, floor edges, suspension members) where brittleness is acceptable
materials.kind: datasheet UD values + engineering estimate (QI rule)

fia.note: 540 GPa ≤ 550 GPa nominal modulus cap; 1.91 ≤ 1.92 g/cm³ density cap: just inside both

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy prepreg, ultra-high modulus (M60J class), quasi-isotropic
materials.typical_f1_use: none on a legal car (space structures)
materials.kind: datasheet UD values + engineering estimate (QI rule)

fia.note: fibre modulus 588 GPa > 550 GPa and density 1.93 > 1.92 g/cm³: outside the permitted carbon-fibre limits

materials.name: Aramid/epoxy (Kevlar 49 class), quasi-isotropic
materials.typical_f1_use: anti-splinter and prescribed laminates (PL-HALO KC60, PL-HEADREST), wheel tethers, fairings
materials.kind: handbook UD values + engineering estimate (QI rule)

fia.note: aramid fibres are permitted reinforcing; the prescribed laminates PL-HALO [KC60, CC100, KC60] and PL-HEADREST [KC60, KC60] use KC60 aramid cloth only (C15.5.2); KC170 is defined in C15.5.1(c) but used by neither

materials.name: PBO/epoxy (Zylon HM class), quasi-isotropic
materials.typical_f1_use: survival-cell side anti-intrusion panels, anti-splinter layers
materials.kind: engineering estimate (UD lamina estimated from fibre values; QI rule)
materials.basis: UD E1 ≈ 0.59 × fibre modulus, UD strength ≈ 0.43 × fibre strength (estimates); then _meta.laminate_rule

fia.note: poly(p-phenylene benzobisoxazole) fibres are permitted reinforcing

materials.name: E-glass/epoxy, quasi-isotropic

materials.kind: handbook UD values + engineering estimate (QI rule)

fia.note: glass fibres limited to types E, S, Q and BF (ISO 2078:2022)

materials.name: Aluminium honeycomb core (5052, 1/8 in cell, 3.1 lb/ft³)
materials.typical_f1_use: survival cell sandwich core (mandatory in the homologated sandwich laminates, ≥ 6 mm), floor and wing sandwich cores
materials.basis: E and strength are out-of-plane stabilised compressive values (cores carry shear and compression, not in-plane tension)

fia.note: the core of every homologated survival-cell sandwich laminate must be aluminium honeycomb ≥ 6 mm thick

materials.name: Meta-aramid (Nomex) honeycomb core (1/8 in cell, 3.0 lb/ft³)

fia.note: meta-aramid honeycomb is a permitted core (not in the survival cell's homologated sandwich laminates, which need aluminium)

materials.name: Stainless steel 17-4PH (H900)
materials.typical_f1_use: skids (C3.6.3(d)(iv), ≤ 38 HRC when new), fittings
materials.basis: H900 condition typical values (skids must be softer than H900: ≤ 38 HRC)

fia.note: iron alloys: any; specific modulus 25.3

materials.name: Maraging steel 18Ni(300), aged
materials.typical_f1_use: gears, shafts, highly loaded pins; also usable as ballast

fia.note: iron alloys: any; density 8000 kg/m³ > 7500 satisfies C4.3.2(d) for driver ballast

materials.name: Nickel superalloy Inconel 718 (aged)
materials.typical_f1_use: exhaust and turbo hardware (PU), high-temperature fasteners

fia.note: UNS N07718 listed

materials.name: Tungsten heavy alloy (≈ 95 % W, W-Ni-Fe, ASTM B777 class 3)
materials.typical_f1_use: ballast (free and driver ballast): the densest practical choice
materials.basis: density mid of the B777 class 3 band 17.75-18.35 g/cm³; tensile = the class minimum; E typical (estimate)

fia.note: tungsten alloys: any, outside the PU; excluded from the PU as a tungsten-base alloy (C15.6.1(g)); at 18,000 kg/m³ it is under the 18,400 kg/m³ PU density limit, so C15.6.1(l) does not apply; > 7500 kg/m³ as C4.3.2(d) wants for driver ballast

materials.name: Particulate-reinforced aluminium MMC (SupremEX 225XE)
materials.typical_f1_use: uprights (C15.3.3(iii)), stiff brackets and housings
materials.basis: Materion typical values (tensile 535-620 MPa by product form; 610 used)

fia.note: specific modulus 39.9 GPa/(g/cm³): just under the C15.1.4 cap of 40; not allowed in the Primary Roll Structure (C15.3.4)

materials.name: Aluminium-beryllium alloy (AlBeMet AM162)
materials.typical_f1_use: none on a legal car (banned in F1 since the early 2000s; aerospace optics)

fia.note: specific modulus 93 GPa/(g/cm³) > 40 (C15.1.4), and not in the C15.2.1 list

materials.name: Carbon-carbon composite (brake / clutch friction grade)
materials.typical_f1_use: brake discs and pads, clutch plates
materials.basis: order-of-magnitude values for a friction-grade C/C; the concept never designs with it

fia.note: carbon-carbon may be used for friction materials only
